values: RTMS Exception Inventory and Refactor Plan
Read-only audit of backend exception creation/handling and frontend error patterns. No source code was changed. Evidence is based on the current working tree scan.
All unchecked failures fall through to a not-found response; business conflicts and unexpected failures can be reported as 404 with raw exception text.
Replace with explicit domain exception hierarchy and a safe default 500 response; preserve a stable error envelope.
Central blast radius. This is the first refactor checkpoint before changing individual services.
The API exposes several paths for status and error-code mapping; ResponseStatusException uses status heuristics and maps every 409 to INVALID_REVIEW_STATE.
Centralize mapping in one exception-to-problem-details policy with domain error codes owned by the domain layer.
Affects client behavior even when HTTP status is correct.
Service and controller code must know transport-level HTTP status, coupling business logic to REST concerns.
Split domain exceptions from an adapter-level HTTP mapping; keep error code and safe message as domain data.
Existing custom exception is useful as an inventory anchor but is transport-coupled.
Many repositories use generic RuntimeException for missing horse, course, stall, task, report, plan, treatment or subject; semantics are implicit and inconsistent.
Introduce typed NotFound exceptions by aggregate/resource and replace generic orElseThrow lambdas incrementally.
Representative examples: HorseService:132, StableStallService:49, GroomDailyTaskService:123, CourseService:42.
IllegalArgumentException for validation and business rules
Input validation, missing related resources, duplicate data and business constraints share the same exception type and often bypass structured field errors.
Use request validation for shape errors and typed domain exceptions for business rule violations; define a stable error-code catalog.
State conflicts such as occupied stall, duplicate review, locked horse, invalid admission state and cancelled workout are not represented as conflict/unprocessable semantics consistently.
Introduce Conflict/InvalidState domain exceptions mapped to 409 or 422 according to a documented matrix.
Groom admission logic is closer to an HTTP contract but keeps transport exceptions in the service and duplicates status/message decisions.
Move admission review outcomes to named domain errors and let one adapter map them to the existing workflow contract.
Keep current API behavior during migration because Groom UI depends on these statuses.
Mixed generic exceptions across review stages
Manager and Trainer review paths use IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException and RuntimeException for equivalent workflow outcomes.
Create one admission-review exception vocabulary shared by Groom, Trainer, Vet and Manager stages.
Important for cross-role consistency and idempotent review actions.
Bare Optional.orElseThrow makes the error type and API response dependent on the global fallback instead of the admission contract.
Replace with explicit typed not-found or invariant exceptions and add controller contract tests.
Security errors have separate servlet and MVC handlers
Unauthorized and forbidden responses are generated in multiple places; message text and logging policy can drift.
Define one error response factory and shared security error codes; keep servlet entry-point integration thin.
Do not merge authentication and authorization semantics; only unify the response contract.
Validation handler returns only first error
Multiple field violations are collapsed into a single message, limiting frontend correction and observability.
Return structured field errors while preserving the existing top-level code/message for compatibility.
Also review MethodArgumentTypeMismatch and malformed JSON responses together.
Database/persistence exceptions are normalized without correlation detail
The client gets a safe message, but server-side diagnostics and constraint-specific classification are not visible in this handler.
Add correlation ID and structured server logging; classify known integrity conflicts separately from unknown database failures.
No raw SQL is returned here, which is good; preserve that behavior.
Storage failures are converted to transport exceptions inside a service; cleanup also ignores IOException, making diagnosis and retry behavior unclear.
Introduce storage-specific exceptions, explicit cleanup logging and a stable error code for unavailable documents.
Review external-hosted document branch separately from local file branch.
Scheduled job failures are swallowed/logged at a broad boundary; partial work and retry policy are not represented in an error contract.
Define job-level failure policy: transaction boundary, retry/backoff, alerting and idempotency key per job run.
This is not an API exception but is part of the refactor surface.
Request continues / audit behavior depends on implementation
Audit failures can be hidden and may not carry request correlation, actor or endpoint context consistently.
Use a dedicated audit failure policy: never break business requests, but emit structured logs/metrics with correlation data.
Keep audit isolation explicit and tested.
RuntimeException wraps token hashing and user lookup
Infrastructure failure and missing user are represented with generic runtime exceptions; auth failures can be misclassified.
Separate authentication failure, missing principal and cryptographic infrastructure exceptions; never expose internal cause text.
Review together with CustomAuthEntryPoint and refresh-token errors.
Incident validation, missing entities, state transitions and attachment errors use multiple generic types and include Vietnamese messages.
Define incident-report validation, not-found, conflict and attachment error codes; keep user-facing language at the API boundary.
Relevant to the recent Groom incident-report UI issue.
Large service owns many generic business exceptions
Plan creation, assignment, scheduling, workout completion and capacity rules share one service and generic exception vocabulary.
Split by use case/domain policy first, then migrate exceptions to typed rule violations without changing behavior in one step.
High change surface; refactor after the central error contract is defined.
Some modules already use ApiException consistently
These services provide a useful migration reference, but error-code naming and 400 vs 409 choices still need a shared catalog.
Use these modules as compatibility baselines; standardize codes and response payload shape before broad migration.
Positive existing pattern, recorded so refactor does not regress it.
Generic Error plus ad hoc catch UI
Frontend services throw generic Error/ApiError and components handle failures independently; message extraction and retry presentation can diverge.
Expose a typed client error model, centralized message mapping and shared loading/error/retry state components.
Secondary scope: inventory only; no frontend changes were made.
Tests lock in RuntimeException/IllegalStateException/IllegalArgumentException instead of the intended HTTP error contract for many paths.
Add controller/API contract tests first, then update service tests to assert typed domain errors and invariants.
Mixed English and Vietnamese exception messages
Message is returned in several handlers
Client-visible error messages are not language-neutral and may expose implementation/business details directly.
Use stable error codes plus localized client messages; keep server logs detailed and client payloads safe.
Examples include HorseService, StableStallService, HorseTrainingPlanService and RaceRegistrationService.
